subject: SIG/CAIQ evidence request — targeted log retention carveout for LyraIO

From: Sara Patel <sara@lyraio.com>

Subject: Request: targeted log retention carveout and SIG/CAIQ evidence for LyraIO

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we prepare for our internal SIG/CAIQ review, Legal and Compliance at LyraIO are asking for a narrow carveout to the standard 180d debug log TTL for a subset of tenant event traces used in fraud investigations. The ask is to retain tenant-scoped debug traces for up to 24 months for (a) flagged fraud investigations and (b) post-incident forensics.

What we need from Redwood:
- SIG mapping: which SIG/CAIQ controls reference log retention and where Redwood's current configuration shows 180d TTL (we can map to CAIQ questions).
- Evidence artifacts: retention_mapping.csv (tenant tag -> retention TTL), proof-of-delete procedure, sampling/export playbook for ad-hoc longer-retain tenants.
- Compensating controls: if you deny a blanket 24-month TTL, we need a list of compensating controls (encrypted at-rest segmentation, limited access roles, keystore residency notes).
- Proposed timeline & gating: how would this be scoped (account-level approval, signed addendum, or SOC2 control exception)?

Attached is our redline of the MSA excerpt and examples of the tenant list scope (attachment: lyraio_msa_redline.pdf). We would like to collect the artifacts by Aug 31 to get them into our SIG evidence binder ahead of the customer review. Can Redwood provide a single artifact package + one 45-min workshop to walk controls?

Appreciate a status and any immediate blockers.

Best,
Sara Patel
Head of Compliance, LyraIO

Hi Sara —

Thank you — we can support a scoped evidence package and a controls walkthrough. Looping in Karthik (SRE/security) and Neha (Security Assurance) to provide the mapping and the tech artifacts.

Quick clarifications so we scope correctly:
1) When you say "tenant-scoped debug traces" — can you confirm the exact event types and the tenant IDs (or a representative sample)? We prefer to avoid open-ended "all debug logs" requests.
2) Is LyraIO requesting a policy change (default retention) or a per-account exception (signed addendum)? Our usual options: addendum + feature flag to mark accounts for extended retention; or we can propose an escrow/secure export workflow if permanent retention is not acceptable.

Deliverables we will aim to produce by Aug 31 if scope is clear:
- SIG/CAIQ crosswalk doc (high level mapping)
- retention_mapping.csv (sample format)
- proof-of-delete SOP (steps + automation hooks)
- compensating controls memo + list of roles with narrower access
- 45-min controls workshop (dates below)

Proposed workshop slots (PDT): Aug 27 10:00, Aug 28 14:00, Aug 31 09:00 — let me know what works.

Attaching our internal checklist to clarify artifacts (Attachment: redwood_retention_checklist.xlsx).

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan | Senior Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference

Sara / Priya —

Quick technical note from SRE/security on what we can deliver and the suggested approach:

What we can provide immediately:
- retention_mapping.csv (sample) that shows data namespace, tenant tag, default TTL, and exception TTL; we will include a small sample of LyraIO tenant IDs after you provide the list.
- proof-of-delete SOP + automation snippet showing delete job and keystore rotation hooks.
- CAIQ pointers: we will call out answers to V2.1/Control area: Logging & Monitoring, Evidence IDs for SOC2 artifact buckets (log-archive, delete-audit).

Suggested scoping model (recommended):
1) Per-account extended retention flag (feature-guarded) — requires LyraIO-signed addendum + RBAC exception (only Compliance PoC and Redwood incident response roles can access extended logs).
2) Access & encryption controls: logs for extended-ttl accounts will be placed in a tenant-tagged bucket encrypted with a separate key (keystore-residency noted). KMS access policies will be included in the compensating controls doc.
3) Periodic sampling & export: we propose a quarterly attestation export to LyraIO-controlled storage and a 30-day retention for exports, as an alternative to indefinite retention.

Caveats / blockers:
- We do not change global default TTL without legal sign-off.
- Forensics copies increase egress/costs; if LyraIO wants on-demand rehydration beyond 180d we will need a funded committed support plan or reserved capacity for long-term archiving.

I'll attach the working file and a short memo. If this scope looks correct, Priya and Neha can produce the formal SIG crosswalk and evidence artifacts.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
